theorem norm_integral_le_of_norm_le {f : α → G} {g : α → ℝ} (hg : Integrable g μ)
    (h : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ g x) : ‖∫ x, f x ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ x, g x ∂μ :=
  calc
    ‖∫ x, f x ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ x, ‖f x‖ ∂μ := norm_integral_le_integral_norm f
    _ ≤ ∫ x, g x ∂μ := integral_mono_of_nonneg (Eventually.of_forall fun _ => norm_nonneg _) hg h

rag.name: MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_integral_norm
rag.content:
theorem norm_integral_le_integral_norm (f : α → G) : ‖∫ a, f a ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ a, ‖f a‖ ∂μ := by
  have le_ae : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, 0 ≤ ‖f a‖ := Eventually.of_forall fun a => norm_nonneg _
  by_cases h : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ
  · calc
      ‖∫ a, f a ∂μ‖ ≤ ENNReal.toReal (∫⁻ a, ENNReal.ofReal ‖f a‖ ∂μ) :=
        norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm _
      _ = ∫ a, ‖f a‖ ∂μ := (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae le_ae <| h.norm).symm
  · rw [integral_non_aestronglyMeasurable h, norm_zero]
    exact integral_nonneg_of_ae le_ae

  simp_rw [← ofReal_norm_eq_enorm]
  apply ENNReal.ofReal_le_of_le_toReal
  exact norm_integral_le_lintegral_norm f

rag.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_ofReal_le_lintegral_enorm
rag.content:
theorem lintegral_ofReal_le_lintegral_enorm (f : α → ℝ) :
    ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal (f x) ∂μ ≤ ∫⁻ x, ‖f x‖ₑ ∂μ := by
  simp_rw [← ofReal_norm_eq_enorm]
  refine lintegral_mono fun x => ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal ?_
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs]
  exact le_abs_self (f x)

informal_statement: The norm of the approximation of a function on a cube is less than or equal to the approximation of the norm of the function on the same cube.
informal_proof:
To prove this, we consider the norm of the approximation of the function on the cube. By breaking down the norm into a sum over the cube, we can apply the property that the norm of a sum is less than or equal to the sum of norms. 

Next, we observe that the norm of an indicator function of the cube multiplied by the function is less than or equal to the indicator function of the cube multiplied by the norm of the function. This step utilizes the fact that norms are positively homogeneous and satisfy the triangle inequality.

Finally, by applying the integral property of norms, we conclude that the norm of the approximation of the function on the cube does not exceed the approximation of the norm of the function on the same cube.

C1_dependencies.name: Disjoint
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Two elements of a lattice are disjoint if their inf is the bottom element.
  (This generalizes disjoint sets, viewed as members of the subset lattice.)

Note that we define this without reference to `⊓`, as this allows us to talk about orders where
the infimum is not unique, or where implementing `Inf` would require additional `Decidable`
arguments. -/
def Disjoint (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ≤ a → x ≤ b → x ≤ ⊥

theorem average_union_mem_openSegment {f : α → E} {s t : Set α} (hd : AEDisjoint μ s t)
    (ht : NullMeasurableSet t μ) (hs₀ : μ s ≠ 0) (ht₀ : μ t ≠ 0) (hsμ : μ s ≠ ∞) (htμ : μ t ≠ ∞)
    (hfs : IntegrableOn f s μ) (hft : IntegrableOn f t μ) :
    ⨍ x in s ∪ t, f x ∂μ ∈ openSegment ℝ (⨍ x in s, f x ∂μ) (⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ) := by
  replace hs₀ : 0 < (μ s).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hs₀ hsμ
  replace ht₀ : 0 < (μ t).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos ht₀ htμ
  exact mem_openSegment_iff_div.mpr
    ⟨(μ s).toReal, (μ t).toReal, hs₀, ht₀, (average_union hd ht hsμ htμ hfs hft).symm⟩

theorem average_union {f : α → E} {s t : Set α} (hd : AEDisjoint μ s t) (ht : NullMeasurableSet t μ)
    (hsμ : μ s ≠ ∞) (htμ : μ t ≠ ∞) (hfs : IntegrableOn f s μ) (hft : IntegrableOn f t μ) :
    ⨍ x in s ∪ t, f x ∂μ =
      ((μ s).toReal / ((μ s).toReal + (μ t).toReal)) • ⨍ x in s, f x ∂μ +
        ((μ t).toReal / ((μ s).toReal + (μ t).toReal)) • ⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ := by
  haveI := Fact.mk hsμ.lt_top; haveI := Fact.mk htμ.lt_top
  rw [restrict_union₀ hd ht, average_add_measure hfs hft, restrict_apply_univ, restrict_apply_univ]

  simp only [setAverage_eq, setIntegral_congr_set h, measure_congr h]

rag.name: MeasureTheory.average_union_mem_segment
rag.content:
theorem average_union_mem_segment {f : α → E} {s t : Set α} (hd : AEDisjoint μ s t)
    (ht : NullMeasurableSet t μ) (hsμ : μ s ≠ ∞) (htμ : μ t ≠ ∞) (hfs : IntegrableOn f s μ)
    (hft : IntegrableOn f t μ) :
    ⨍ x in s ∪ t, f x ∂μ ∈ [⨍ x in s, f x ∂μ -[ℝ] ⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ] := by
  by_cases hse : μ s = 0
  · rw [← ae_eq_empty] at hse
    rw [restrict_congr_set (hse.union EventuallyEq.rfl), empty_union]
    exact right_mem_segment _ _ _
  · refine
      mem_segment_iff_div.mpr
        ⟨(μ s).toReal, (μ t).toReal, ENNReal.toReal_nonneg, ENNReal.toReal_nonneg, ?_,
          (average_union hd ht hsμ htμ hfs hft).symm⟩
    calc
      0 < (μ s).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_pos hse hsμ
      _ ≤ _ := le_add_of_nonneg_right ENNReal.toReal_nonneg

rag.name: MeasureTheory.laverage
rag.content:
/-- Average value of an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function `f` w.r.t. a measure `μ`, denoted `⨍⁻ x, f x ∂μ`.

It is equal to `(μ univ)⁻¹ * ∫⁻ x, f x ∂μ`, so it takes value zero if `μ` is an infinite measure. If
`μ` is a probability measure, then the average of any function is equal to its integral.

For the average on a set, use `⨍⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ`, defined as `⨍⁻ x, f x ∂(μ.restrict s)`. For the
average w.r.t. the volume, one can omit `∂volume`. -/
noncomputable def laverage (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) := ∫⁻ x, f x ∂(μ univ)⁻¹ • μ

rag.name: MeasureTheory.average_add_measure
rag.content:
theorem average_add_measure [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {ν : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure ν] {f : α → E}
    (hμ : Integrable f μ) (hν : Integrable f ν) :
    ⨍ x, f x ∂(μ + ν) =
      ((μ univ).toReal / ((μ univ).toReal + (ν univ).toReal)) • ⨍ x, f x ∂μ +
        ((ν univ).toReal / ((μ univ).toReal + (ν univ).toReal)) • ⨍ x, f x ∂ν := by
  simp only [div_eq_inv_mul, mul_smul, measure_smul_average, ← smul_add,
    ← integral_add_measure hμ hν, ← ENNReal.toReal_add (measure_ne_top μ _) (measure_ne_top ν _)]
  rw [average_eq, Measure.add_apply]

rag.name: MeasureTheory.laverage_union
rag.content:
theorem laverage_union (hd : AEDisjoint μ s t) (ht : NullMeasurableSet t μ) :
    ⨍⁻ x in s ∪ t, f x ∂μ =
      μ s / (μ s + μ t) * ⨍⁻ x in s, f x ∂μ + μ t / (μ s + μ t) * ⨍⁻ x in t, f x ∂μ := by
  rw [restrict_union₀ hd ht, laverage_add_measure, restrict_apply_univ, restrict_apply_univ]

informal_statement: For any set of disjoint grid cubes \( C \) and a function \( f \) defined on the points of the grid, the value of the function \( \text{approxOnCube}\ C\ f \) at any point \( x \) inside a cube \( J \) is equal to the average value of \( f \) over that cube \( J \).
informal_proof:
To establish the equality \( (\text{approxOnCube}\ C\ f)(x) = \⨍ y \in J, f(y) \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Decompose the Sum**: By definition, \( \text{approxOnCube}\ C\ f(x) \) is expressed as a sum over all cubes in \( C \), each multiplied by an indicator function that selects the cube containing \( x \).

2. **Vanishing Terms**: Due to the disjointness of the cubes in \( C \), the only term in the sum that does not vanish is the one corresponding to the cube \( J \) that contains \( x \). All other terms cancel out because no other cube intersects with \( J \).

3. **Focus on the Relevant Cube**: The remaining term is the average of \( f \) over the cube \( J \), weighted by the indicator function. Since \( x \) lies within \( J \), this term simplifies to the desired average \( \⨍ y \in J, f(y) \).

Thus, \( \text{approxOnCube}\ C\ f(x) \) indeed equals the average of \( f \) over the cube \( J \) containing \( x \).
